findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid legacy prefixed values
findings.body: The mixin passes `$alignment` unchanged to `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. The legacy syntaxes use different keywords: `center` is valid, but `baseline` is valid only for some and `flex-start` and `flex-end` must be `start` and `end`. Because `badges.css.scss` calls `align-items(baseline)`, the old prefixed declarations can be invalid or wrong on older browsers. `-ms-align-items` is not a real property. The `-moz-box-ordinal-group` in `order` is also not a valid flex ordering fallback, since it only applies to the old box model.

findings.title: Invalid inline-flex vendor prefixes
findings.body: The mixin emits `display: -moz-inline-box` and `-webkit-inline-box`, which map to the old box model and are not equivalent to inline-flex. The old `-webkit-inline-box` is paired with `-webkit-box-align`, but nothing else in the mixin follows the old-box syntax, so the fallback behaves inconsistently. It also sets `-moz-box` for `flexbox`, which does not provide the intended layout.

findings.title: Header layout changes may break the title and panel arrangement
findings.body: The `.title` float rule was removed and `.contents` became a flex container, and `.panel` now uses `margin-left: auto` plus `order(3)`. Any child without an explicit order (for example the title or the extra-info wrapper, which has order 2) now depends on flex ordering. The `.valign-helper` with `height: 100%` is now a flex item and may render oddly. The `.icons`, `.login-button` and similar floats inside the panel are still floated, so the panel's height may collapse without a clearfix.

findings.title: small-action flex change leaves floats and clear in place
findings.body: `.small-action` becomes a flex container, but its children still use `float: left` and `float: right` (the avatar, the button and the custom message). Floats are ignored on flex items, so the intended right alignment of the button is lost and it sits next to the description. The `clear: both` is still there. The padding changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, and the removed margins and padding alter the spacing of the text.

findings.title: order() is applied to an element that may not be a flex item
findings.body: `.extra-info-wrapper` gets `order(2)`, which has an effect only if its parent is a flex container. The parent is not shown to be one in this change. The removed `margin-top: 5px` for `.bullet` badges may also misalign bullets, because the new `line-height: 1.5` is set on the wrapper but the bullet badge uses `inline-flex` with baseline alignment.
